label: early original-phase step after a 3/l/g/q-initial sequence, on input n/1/0/f/z/j-like tokens
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (97% of mass), at t=2..7 (peak at t=3-4), never at t=0-1. Silent in the copy phase; small activity on <DEL> right after such prefixes. It behaves like an additive mix of the sequence prefix and the current token. The prefix contributes when the sequence starts with 3, l, g or q (first_tok=3 has 9.6x lift, l 6.4x), or when l/r/g/3 appear two steps back. The current token contributes when it is n, 1, 0, f, z or j (about 4x lift), and the step is mostly the first occurrence of that token. The strongest activations (n, 1 or z at t=3-4 after prefixes like 3 l / 3 3 / l l) need both. Taking both conditions together gives dev F1 about 0.45 and mass recall 0.68. Many activations come from just one strong part (for example d r [0]), and many steps that meet both conditions stay silent. So this is a graded, distributed code rather than a crisp category. It does not fire on letters like a, c, e, t, w as the current input, or at late positions.
